rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods <U+2013> 2-year split-plot field experiment in Corvallis, OR, with three irrigation systems (sprinkler, microspray, drip) and three irrigation levels, replicated five times. Q2: Table 4 and Abstract <U+2013> drip-irrigated 'Duke' blueberry had 14.3% roots infected by Phytophthora cinnamomi versus 6.7<U+2013>7.3% under sprinklers and microsprays, with half the shoot and root dry weight and lower root system vigor; Discussion states drip likely increased root rot because it maintained higher soil water content. Q3: Results <U+2013> root rot established by laboratory plating of root segments on selective media (P5ARP+H, isolates identified as P. cinnamomi) and independently by field root-system vigor ratings, canopy cover imaging and visual symptoms (premature red/yellow leaves, stunted shoots), with regression linking vigor to infection (Fig. 4B). Q4: Table 2 and Fig. 1 <U+2013> volumetric soil water content measured by TDR in top 0.3 m; drip held 5<U+2013>6% higher soil water than sprinklers/microsprays in 2005, often above field capacity, identified as the mechanism for greater infection. Q7: Summary paragraph <U+2013> authors state from their results that sites prone to root rot (heavy soil, poor drainage, disease history) are less suited to drip, and that soil saturation occurred when drip was applied at 100<U+2013>150% ETc on the silty clay loam.
rows.notes: Single site, single cultivar ('Duke'), one soil type (silty clay loam), plot scale; no multi-site or farm-scale evidence. Q3 answered yes with some doubt: root vigor ratings and growth measures are symptom-based and could partly reflect waterlogging rather than pathogen infection, but the study treats them as independent disease-severity measures alongside culture-based isolation. Q8: the paper notes uncertainty about inoculum origin and that 'Duke' is highly susceptible, and calls for further study of drip lateral placement/frequency, but does not state limitations of its own drip<U+2013>root rot result (single site, cultivar, duration), so answered no. Q9: only letter groupings, P-values and R<U+00B2> reported; no SD/SE/CI visible in the text.
